plan.topic: A bruise where you injected tirzepatide: what the label counts as an injection-site reaction, why rotating sites is advised in the Instructions for Use, and when a mark needs a call
plan.angle:
08:00 calm 'Is this normal?' visible pen moment. Follow the task's length arm and hook archetype.
- Sentence 1 (14 words or fewer): 'Tirzepatide shot left a small bruise? Here's what the label counts.' Scene 1's on-screen text matches it.
- By 6 s, the relief fact goes in the same line, with no standalone validation sentence: bruising is one of the terms the Zepbound label groups under injection-site reactions, 6–8% by dose vs about 2% on placebo. Copy the term list exactly from the label (PI rev. 28 Aug 2026, section 6.1).
- Credit 'change (rotate) your injection site each week' only to the single-dose pen IFU at its own URL, quoted only if it loads.
- Untagged red flags: spreading redness, warmth, pus or fever means call your prescriber.
- In label wording: swelling of the face, lips or throat, or trouble breathing, means your local emergency number right away. Then 'For anything that isn't one of those emergency signs, don't stop or change your medicine on your own.'
- Scope card: 'US single-dose pen; KwikPens and vials have their own leaflets.'
- No technique beyond the IFU, no doses.
- Close with 'Not personal advice, so ask your prescriber.' and a line that loops back to sentence 1. No subscribe line, no link line.
- Post note: the related-video target is the Pen how-to video.

plan.why: Visible injection-site moments are our proven Short winners (254, 202 and 159 views). A bruise is the one skin moment not yet covered on its own, and the Short feeds the Pen how-to video once its related-video link is set.

package.title: Tirzepatide Shot Bruise? What the Label Says #shorts
package.description:
The Zepbound label groups bruising under injection-site reactions. Mounjaro's label lists injection-site reactions too, and both labels say to rotate your injection site with each dose.
If your face, lips or throat swell, or you have trouble breathing, call your local emergency number right away. For anything that isn't one of those emergency signs, don't stop or change your medicine on your own.
#tirzepatide
Not personal advice. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

factcheck.summary:
This Short passes. I opened both US labels (each shows Revised: 8/2026), and every factual claim matches them:
- **Bruising:** the Zepbound label §6.1 lists bruising among the terms grouped under injection-site reactions.
- **The numbers:** in the two placebo-controlled weight trials (Studies 1 and 2, up to 72 weeks), injection-site reactions were reported in 6% on 5 mg, 8% on 10 mg and 8% on 15 mg, versus 2% on placebo. So "6–8% by dose vs ~2% placebo" is correct.
- **Rotation:** both labels say in §2: "Rotate injection sites with each dose."
- **Mounjaro:** its label §6.1 does list injection-site reactions (3.2% vs 0.4% placebo, in a different pool of trials). The script never says Mounjaro's label mentions bruising, which is correct, because it doesn't.

The script doesn't claim that rotating sites reduces bruising. The population on the card is complete, and the safety lines and closing follow channel rules. My count of the spoken words matches the stated 148, inside the 135–160 arm. Three minor wording fixes are listed below; with them applied the Short can ship.

issues.claim: In two weight trials, those were reported in 6 to 8 percent of people on Zepbound, by dose.
issues.problem: The spoken line gives no placebo comparison (it's only on the card), which breaks the rule that every number names its comparator. 'Those' is also an unclear referent for listeners who missed S1-2.
issues.fix: In two weight trials, injection-site reactions were reported in 6 to 8 percent of people on Zepbound, by dose, versus about 2 percent on placebo. (Adds 8 words, for 156 total, still within 135–160.)

issues.claim: If your face, lips or throat swell, or you have trouble breathing, call your local emergency number right away.
issues.problem: Optional and minor. The label's serious allergic reaction signs also include swelling of the tongue and trouble swallowing. Adding them makes the trigger list more complete without changing the fixed structure.
issues.fix: Narration: "If your face, lips, tongue or throat swell, or you have trouble breathing or swallowing, call your local emergency number right away." On-screen: "Face, lips, tongue or throat swelling, or trouble breathing or swallowing: emergency number, right away". (Adds 4 words. If you also apply the S1-3 fix, the total is 160, which is exactly the cap. In that case, drop 'local' to stay at 159.)

issues.problem: Both live pages show only 'Revised: 8/2026'. The exact days match the channel's known dates, so keep them. No change is needed unless the publisher requires the format shown on the page.
issues.fix: Keep as is, or use 'Revised 8/2026' to match the live page exactly.
